observed_structure: BlockMergeSort::sort loads one fixed-size value chunk per thread from threadgroup storage into registers, conditionally carries a matching index chunk, and invokes the configured thread-local sort.
The merge-stage loop doubles merge_threads from two through the configured thread count while keeping the current value and optional index chunks in thread-local registers between stages.

Each stage executes a barrier, has every thread publish its current register chunk to reused threadgroup storage, executes a second barrier, derives the thread's merge group and lane, and addresses two sorted runs.

The stage calls merge_partition and merge_step to replace the thread-local chunks from those runs; after the final stage, another barrier precedes terminal publication of the register chunks to threadgroup storage for the enclosing caller.
variant_notes: Value-only sort and index-carrying argsort share this helper, while block width, values per thread, comparator, dtype initialization, tie and NaN handling, and ordering properties remain outside the observed recurrence.

Single-block versus multi-block dispatch, contiguous versus non-contiguous addressing, initial device-to-threadgroup fill, post-helper synchronization, global output, and host ping-pong are owned by enclosing paths.

Barrier placement and threadgroup reuse do not establish visibility sufficiency, uniform participation, race or deadlock freedom, bounds, memory safety, stability, deterministic ordering, correctness, or performance.
